title: Tenant-aware soft-fallback with hysteresis and grace windows for region/tier routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During regional capacity pressure and transient service errors (429s, return-timeouts, and elevated error-rates), customers experience abrupt hard fallbacks that cause cascaded latency spikes, degraded token quality, and unnecessary cost when large models are used. We need a tenant-aware soft-fallback controller that uses weighted signals, per-tenant QoS profiles, and a configurable hysteresis/grace-window to decide when to (a) soft-throttle, (b) fallback to cheaper model variants, or (c) open circuit breakers for a tenant/region/tier. Goal: reduce noisy hard-cutover events, preserve quality for high-priority tenants, and automatically surface actionable telemetry for SRE/product teams.
acceptance_criteria: Controller evaluates combined signal vector (429 rate, timeout rate, 5xx rate, p95 latency, queue depth) and emits a single fallback decision per tenant-region-tier within 200ms of signal update

Soft-fallback path (priority queueing + model-variant fallback) reduces p95 latency by >=15% for overloaded requests without increasing 99th-percentile model errors more than 5% on synthetic eval prompt-set
Hysteresis: controller must not flip state more than once per 60s per tenant-region-tier under oscillating signals
Telemetry: events and decision traces for each action are emitted to routing-traces and tagged with tenant_id, region, tier, model_id, and version
Feature rollout gate via runtime flag per-customer and canary across 5%/25%/100% cohorts
Unit + integration tests for signal fusion, decay windows, and fallback execution exist and pass in CI
dev_notes: Prototype algorithm: compute a weighted_trip_score = w1*429_rate_norm + w2*timeout_rate_norm + w3*5xx_rate_norm + w4*latency_score where weights are tenant-specific and normalized by historical baselines.
Implement per-tenant QoS profile: priority {gold,silver,bronze} maps to (weights, fallbacks, grace-window). Default profiles seeded from product recommendations.
Hysteresis design: two thresholds (enter, exit) with time-decay on trip_score and a minimum dwell time to avoid flapping.

Decision actions: soft-throttle (reduce concurrency tokens), enqueue to low-priority pool, redirect to model-variant (quantized/sea-1-small), or open circuit (reject with informative 503 + retry-after).
Fallback to model-variant must preserve deterministic KV-cache compatibility or rewarm strategy to avoid large cold-start penalty.
Telemetry: attach 'decision_trace' blob to request logs and to per-tenant dashboard to inspect why a fallback occurred. Ensure PII-free traces.
Edge-case: downstream region-wide outage should prefer cross-region fallback before opening per-tenant circuit for high-priority tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local sim using synthetic workload generator - target end 2026-03-12
Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal team tenants (10%) in us-west-2 for 24h, monitor routing-traces and token-level cost - target 2026-03-16
Phase 2 (broader canary): expand to 25% of production non-enterprise tenants across two regions, run A/B against control for 72h - target 2026-03-20
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 50% -> 100% with 24h monitoring windows and automatic rollback on predefined regression signals
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and a follow-up doc with metrics and tuning recommendations
telemetry_metrics: 429 rate, timeout rate, 5xx rate by tenant-region-tier
customer-facing error rates and SLO breach frequency
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math, hysteresis state machine, and profile loading
Integration test that simulates spike of 429s and verifies soft-throttle path triggers and recovers without flapping
E2E canary harness: compare model output quality on an eval prompt-set for requests that were fallbacked vs. control (target <=5% quality delta for gold; <=10% for silver)
Load test with mixed-tenant weights to validate latency and token cost improvements
